symbols.name: speed of light in vacuum
symbols.note: The book writes c₀ to stress ‘in vacuum’; the lecture writes c.

symbols.name: wavelength in vacuum
symbols.typical: the wavelength you are given, e.g. 650 nm
symbols.note: Inside a medium the wavelength is λ₀/n; formulas with λ₀ want the vacuum value.

symbols.name: absorption-edge wavelength (λ at which E_ph = E_G)
bandgap energy
symbols.note: Same quantity as E_G; the lecture writes both.

symbols.name: irradiation (energy per area)
symbols.typical: ≈ 1000 kWh m⁻² per year in NL

symbols.name: refractive index of the surrounding medium
extinction coefficient (written k in some exercises)
symbols.note: Exercise 7.5 writes ñ = n − ik; the book writes ñ = n + iκ. The sign convention does not change R or α.

symbols.name: absorption coefficient
symbols.typical: c-Si: 2.9 × 10³ cm⁻¹ at 650 nm, 64 cm⁻¹ at 1000 nm

symbols.name: absorptance (fraction of light absorbed in the layer)
penetration depth (1/α)
symbols.typical: c-Si: 3.4 µm at 650 nm, 156 µm at 1000 nm

symbols.name: angle of incidence (from the surface normal)
angle of refraction (transmitted ray, from the normal)
angle of a ray with the surface normal
angle between the Sun and the zenith
critical angle for total internal reflection
angle of the ray after the back reflector (in the absorber)
total reflectance of a coated surface (instruction approach R₁ + R₂)
electric field
symbols.note: The book and lecture use ξ (xi) for the electric field.

symbols.name: spectral irradiance (power per area per wavelength)
symbols.unit: W m⁻² m⁻¹ (often W m⁻² nm⁻¹)
symbols.typical: ≈ 1.5 W m⁻² nm⁻¹ peak of AM1.5

symbols.name: spectral power density P(λ) (lecture notation for I_eλ)
symbols.note: Lecture 1 writes P(λ); the book writes I_eλ. Same quantity.

symbols.name: photon flux density (lecture: Φ(λ) per unit wavelength)
photon flux (density): photons per area per time
incident spectral photon flux
symbols.note: Superscript 0: the flux arriving at the surface (formula sheet eq. 7.3).

symbols.name: radiant emittance of a blackbody (total power emitted per area)
spectral radiance of a blackbody (Planck’s law)
spectral radiance per unit frequency (lecture’s Planck law)
solid angle of the Sun seen from Earth
air mass (relative path length through the atmosphere)
photocurrent density
symbols.typical: ≈ 40 mA cm⁻² for c-Si under AM1.5

symbols.name: decay length
symbols.note: After a distance L an exponential decay has dropped to 1/e ≈ 37 %.

symbols.name: maximum output power (at the maximum power point)
angle of the ray inside the coating
symbols.note: Here c = coating, not ‘critical’; the critical angle is written θ_crit.

symbols.name: angle of the ray in air
Brewster angle (p-reflectance is zero)
symbols.note: Beyond the course: tan θ_B = n₂/n₁.

symbols.name: the lower of the two refractive indices
the higher of the two refractive indices
amplitude reflection coefficient, outside medium → coating
phase thickness of the coating (2π n_c d/λ₀)
wave number along z (2π/λ in the medium)
real part of the wave number
imaginary part of the wave number (attenuation of the field)
electron concentration (density of free electrons)
symbols.typical: ≈ 10¹⁰ cm⁻³ intrinsic Si; ≈ N_D in n-type

symbols.name: effective density of states in the conduction band
effective density of states in the valence band
hole concentration (density of holes)
symbols.typical: ≈ 10¹⁰ cm⁻³ intrinsic Si; ≈ N_A in p-type

symbols.name: density of states in the conduction band
density of states in the valence band
effective mass of electrons
symbols.note: The electron mass corrected for the periodic crystal potential.

symbols.name: Δ: change in, or excess of, the quantity that follows
symbols.note: Δn = n − n₀: excess electron density under illumination.

symbols.name: (minority-carrier) lifetime
symbols.typical: ~1 µs typical c-Si, ~1 ms very pure

symbols.name: generation rate of electrons (other than thermal)
generation rate of holes (other than thermal)
generation quantum efficiency (pairs per absorbed photon)
length: diffusion length, or a given length (ex. 7.7)
Auger coefficient (ehh process); the lecture also writes C_p for the SRH capture coefficient
constant (amplitude or slope) fixed by boundary conditions
recombination rate (or reflectance R in optics parts)
